item.title: One breakdown exposes decades of energy mismanagement
item.description:
A fire at one of Bangladesh’s two floating liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminals has exposed the country’s growing dependence on imported fuel, triggering a nationwide gas crisis that has left households unable to cook, factories struggling to maintain production, power generation reduced and thousands of vehicles stranded in long queues for fuel.
The disruption began after a fire damaged the floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) operated by US-based Excelerate Energy off Maheshkhali in Cox’s Bazar, forcing the terminal to suspend gas supply.
The outage has cut around 450 million cubic feet of gas per day (MMCFD) from the national grid, widening an already significant gap between demand and supply.
Bangladesh currently requires about 3,800 MMCFD of natural gas daily but can supply only 2,700 to 2,800 MMCFD, even under normal conditions.
With nearly 35% to 40% of the country’s gas now coming from imported LNG, the failure of a single import terminal has rippled through almost every sector of the economy.
The ongoing gas crisis across the capital has left city dwellers in a state of distress. Many families are forced to cook on makeshift brick stoves as the gas pressure in the pipeline has dropped. Such scenes were seen in the capital’s Mohammadpur’s Navodaya Housing area on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
The most immediate impact has been felt in households, particularly across Dhaka, where residents in Mirpur, Mohammadpur, Dhanmondi, Badda, Sukrabad, Kalabagan, Kafrul and several other neighbourhoods reported little or no gas supply for weeks.
Many families have abandoned piped gas altogether during peak hours, relying instead on electric stoves, LPG cylinders or traditional clay stoves, pushing up monthly household expenses.
Jhumur Begum of Mirpur said her family had not been able to cook normally for almost a month.
“There were days when my family survived on bread and bananas because we could not cook,” she said, adding that the family eventually bought an electric stove while continuing to pay the monthly gas bill.

Such scenes were seen in the capital’s Mohammadpur’s Navodaya Housing area on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
For parents with young children, the disruption has become particularly difficult.
Akhi Akter, a Mohammadpur resident, said preparing food for her infant has become a daily struggle because gas pressure remains too weak even when supply briefly returns.
The shortage has also paralysed transport services.
Long queues have formed at CNG filling stations across the capital as low pressure has slowed refuelling operations.
Drivers say what once took five minutes now often requires waiting three to four hours, costing them valuable working time and reducing daily earnings.
Many operators say they can no longer fully refill vehicle cylinders because of inadequate pressure, while protests have already erupted in some districts over the prolonged shortages.
The crisis is extending beyond households and transport.
Industrial operators report reduced production as factories struggle with inadequate gas pressure, while officials estimate gas-based electricity generation has already fallen by around 1,500 megawatts, raising concerns about wider disruptions if the shortage continues.

Such scenes were seen in the capital’s Mohammadpur’s Navodaya Housing area on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
Authorities initially expected repairs to restore supply within a few days.
However, several days after technical teams from the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates arrived at the damaged terminal, Petrobangla says no definite timeline can yet be given for resuming full operations.
The state-owned company has apologised to consumers and warned that low gas pressure will continue across the Titas distribution network until the terminal is restored.
Energy experts say the crisis has highlighted a deeper structural weakness in Bangladesh’s energy security.
Domestic gas production has been declining for years while dependence on imported LNG continues to rise, leaving the country increasingly vulnerable to operational failures at a small number of import facilities.
Experts estimate Bangladesh needs additional LNG storage, more regasification capacity and faster domestic exploration to reduce such risks.
The government says it has launched short-, medium- and long-term measures, including drilling 100 new gas wells, exploring new onshore and offshore reserves and establishing another floating LNG terminal.
Even so, officials caution that the country is likely to continue facing a structural gas deficit of 200 to 250 MMCFD even after the damaged terminal resumes operations, meaning the current crisis may ease but the underlying shortage will remain.

item.title: Pedestrian killed as bus ploughs into Kurmitola Hospital compound
item.description:
A pedestrian was killed and two others, including a child, were injured after a passenger bus veered out of control and ploughed into the compound of Kurmitola General Hospital in the capital on Sunday night.
The deceased, Rafiqul Islam, was an employee of a local hotel.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (Gulshan Division) Tanvir Hasan confirmed the incident.
According to police and local sources, the driver of a Poristhan Paribahan bus lost control while attempting to pull over in the Kurmitola area to drop off passengers.
The bus veered into the compound of Kurmitola General Hospital, crashing through part of the wall of a gas control room beside the main gate. Rafiqul Islam, who was standing near the entrance, was struck by the bus and died on the spot.
Police from Cantonment Police Station later detained the bus driver in connection with the incident.

item.title: Gas crisis forces families out of their kitchens
item.description:
Thousands of families across Dhaka have effectively been driven out of their own kitchens as a week-long gas crisis continues to cripple residential supply, forcing many households to rely on restaurants for daily meals while their monthly gas bills continue to arrive.
With piped gas either unavailable or reduced to a weak flame for most of the day, many residents say cooking has become impossible.
While some households have switched to electric stoves, LPG cylinders or even traditional clay stoves, thousands of others -- particularly apartment dwellers -- have been left with no practical alternative but to buy cooked food every day, significantly increasing their living costs.
The crisis has been especially difficult for families with infants and young children, who say preparing fresh meals has become a daily struggle.
The impact is visible across the capital.
Restaurants in Dhanmondi, Shukrabad, Mirpur and Mohammadpur have witnessed an unusual surge in customers from breakfast until late afternoon, with owners saying many neighbourhood families have become regular customers since the gas shortage intensified.
Shabuddin Ahmed, who works at a hotel in Mirpur-10, said business had changed noticeably over the past week.
“Earlier we did not have this many customers. Now the crowds have grown significantly because many people have no gas at home,” he said.
Nibir Ahmed, a private university student living in Dhanmondi, said eating outside had become routine.
“I cannot even remember the last time I cooked at home,” he said, adding that despite living in the area for several years, he had never experienced such a prolonged gas shortage.
For others, the situation has become more severe.
Abida Islam, a resident of Shewrapara, said her family spent several nights surviving on biscuits, bread and bananas because they were unable to cook.
She alleged that despite days of disruption, consumers had received little relief or clear information from the authorities.
The crisis has also transformed the economics of the restaurant business.
Managers at several eateries, including Barishal Hotel, Hanif Biriyani and Lalbag Biriyani in Shukrabad, said customer numbers had risen sharply over the past week.
Some estimated rice consumption had increased by an additional 20 to 25 kilograms daily, while others reported biriyani sales climbing by as much as 40%.
Yet restaurant owners say the boom has come at a price.
Many have been forced to abandon piped gas and switch to expensive LPG cylinders to keep their kitchens running.
Mohammad Nayeem Islam, manager of a restaurant in the area, said the business had spent around Tk600,000 for a gas connection only six months ago but still could not rely on regular supply.
“We now purchase 30 to 40 LPG cylinders every month at around Tk6,600 each. Sales have increased, but so have our costs, leaving us with much smaller profits,” he said.
Some customers alleged that restaurants had stopped selling plain rice separately to maximise earnings, an allegation owners denied, arguing that soaring LPG costs had made simple rice sales financially unviable.
For consumers, however, the financial burden continues to mount.
Abdur Rahim, a Dhanmondi resident, said his family’s monthly food expenses had nearly doubled.
“There is no gas at home, and LPG cylinders are also difficult to find. We have no choice but to buy meals from restaurants every day,” he said.
As repair work continues at the damaged LNG terminal and gas shortages persist across the capital, what began as an energy supply disruption is increasingly becoming a cost-of-living crisis, with thousands of Dhaka families paying twice -- once for gas they cannot use, and again for meals they cannot cook.

Jamaat calls for urgent action to ease gas crisis
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Sunday urged the government and relevant authorities to take immediate and effective measures to resolve the ongoing gas crisis and provide relief to people suffering from the shortage.
In a statement, the party's Assistant Secretary General Advocate Zubair said people across the country are facing an acute shortage of LPG and CNG gas, which are essential commodities.
He expressed deep concern over widespread disruptions to daily cooking, CNG-powered transport services and industrial production due to the crisis.
He also said long queues of vehicles have been seen at CNG stations in the capital because of the severe gas shortage.
"As a result, millions of working hours of citizens are being wasted, and public suffering has reached its peak. People believe that illegal gas connections, government mismanagement, irregularities and syndicates are largely responsible for the crisis," he said.
He demanded an investigation into whether any group was attempting to create an artificial gas shortage to increase prices and urged authorities to take effective measures to reduce public suffering.
Zubair also called for exploring and drilling new gas wells, ensuring extraction from existing wells and securing necessary LNG imports in line with public demand.
He alleged that the government is focused on securing the interests of unscrupulous groups rather than addressing citizens' basic needs, resulting in a severe gas crisis across the country.

item.title: Educational institutions to observe 21 holidays in August, September
item.description:
Teachers and students at educational institutions across the country will observe a total of 21 holidays in August and September, including weekly holidays, according to the academic calendar.
The calendar shows that August will have 9 weekly holidays. In addition, educational institutions will remain closed on August 5 for July Mass Uprising Day, August 12 for Akheri Chahar Somba, and August 26 for Eid-e-Miladunnabi.
In total, educational institutions will observe 12 holidays in August.
September will have 8 weekly holidays. Educational institutions will also remain closed on September 24 for Fateha-i-Yazdaham.
Madhu Purnima and Mahalaya fall on Saturdays and therefore will not be counted as additional holidays.
As a result, educational institutions will observe 9 holidays in September, bringing the combined total for August and September to 21.

item.title: Four bodies recovered in Naogaon within six hours
item.description:
Police recovered the bodies of four people from different parts of Naogaon within a span of six hours on Sunday.
Three of them died after drowning, while the body of another youth was recovered from his home.
In Badalgachhi upazila, Nur Islam, and Sumaiya Akter, drowned in a canal near Kartikahar village while bathing around noon. Locals rescued them and took them to Badalgachhi Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared them dead.
Nur was from Gangni upazila of Meherpur, while Sumaiya was the daughter of Shahin Hossain of Kartikahar village.
Badalgachhi Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Muhammad Ruhul Amin said the bodies were handed over to the families without autopsies following their applications.
In Raninagar, farmer Abdul Mondal, drowned after falling from a boat in a waterbody in Belbari village while returning home after cutting grass for cattle. His body was recovered after about three and a half hours of search by locals and a Fire Service diving team.
Raninagar Police Station OC Md Zakaria Mondal said the body was handed over to the family without an autopsy following their request.
Meanwhile, police recovered the body of Limon Hasan, from his room in Bandhaikhara Sardarpara area of Atrai upazila in the morning.
Police said Limon’s family found him dead after breaking open the door when he did not respond in the morning. His body was sent to Naogaon Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy.
Atrai Police Station OC Mahbub Alam said police recovered the body and sent it to Naogaon Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy.
“An unnatural death case has been filed and the incident is being investigated,” he said.

item.title: 'Use Nazrul Barsho logo on official letters until May 2027'
item.description:
The Cabinet Division has directed all government offices to use the designated logo of ‘Nazrul Barsho’ in official letters until May 25, 2027.
A letter containing the instruction was sent on Sunday to the senior secretaries and secretaries of all ministries and divisions, divisional commissioners, deputy commissioners (DCs) and all Upazila Nirbahi Officers (UNOs).
The letter said the government has declared the period from May 25, 2026 to May 25, 2027 as ‘Nazrul Barsho’.
On the occasion, the Prime Minister unveiled the designated logo of ‘Nazrul Barsho’ on July 2.
It further said that, as part of efforts to uphold the ideals, spirit and literary works of national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam in the thoughts and actions of the nation and to observe ‘Nazrul Barsho’ with due dignity, the Ministry of Cultural Affairs requested the use of the designated logo on all official letters until May 25, 2027.

item.title: IUB book discussion explores how grandmothers keep family stories alive
item.description:
The anthology "Stories My Grandma (Never) Told Me" transforms the oral histories women have long shared in kitchens and family gatherings into a lasting literary record, academics and writers said at a book discussion hosted by Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB) on Sunday.
The book edited by Professor Razia Sultana Khan of IUB was discussed at an event organised by the Department of English and Modern Languages at the DMK Lecture Gallery of IUB.
Speaking as a discussant, Professor Firdous Azim of BRAC University said the anthology carried personal resonance for her as a grandmother herself.
She said her six-year-old granddaughter sleeps beside her every night waiting to hear stories, an experience that revived her own memories of tales told by her grandmothers.
Reading and writing in English, she said, allows such stories to be passed on to students and offers them a wider perspective on family and history.
Iftekhar Ahmed Chowdhury, president of the Cosmos Foundation and former Foreign Affairs Adviser, described the book as a tribute that turns the "whispers of resilience" and unspoken truths of women into a powerful "chorus," arguing that domestic spaces such as kitchens and funerals are where history is truly forged.
Calling the volume a "vibrant tapestry," he said while the book celebrates oral history, the figure of the grandmother often serves as a metaphor through which the authors channel their own contemporary reflections.
He recommended the book not merely as a record of the past but as a portrait of the writers themselves, saying the grandmothers in its pages, real or imagined, remain the "keepers of us."
Sayyeda Tun Noor Sameera, a faculty member at IUB, called the anthology a beautifully produced and accessible volume, noting that an English-language book of this kind published in Bangladesh remains a rare occurrence.
She said editor Razia had brought together the everyday stories grandmothers commonly tell their grandchildren, adding that such stories leave a lasting imprint on children's nostalgic memories and that the bond between grandmother and grandchild, built through storytelling, evokes something akin to seeking nirvana.
Elita Karim, musician and a PhD student at Arizona State University, reflected on the role women play in passing down knowledge and memory through stories, music and poetry, saying the anthology captures this tradition as an art form in its own right.
Following the discussion, editor Razia Sultana Khan introduced the contributing writers to the audience.
According to the book's flap copy, the stories in the anthology are written by members of The Reading Circle (TRC), a community of readers spanning continents, genres and cultures who have previously translated works by Kazi Nazrul Islam and Alice Munro and compiled personal narratives in "Stories from the Edge: Personal Narratives of 1971."
The new collection grew out of the group's fascination with the family secrets and hidden histories that persist across generations, resurfacing much like banned books circulated underground.

item.title: Nur: Govt working to resolve UAE visa issues
item.description:
The government is working to resolve visa-related issues affecting Bangladeshi workers seeking employment in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Haque Nur has said.
In a Facebook post on Sunday, the state minister said the government is aware of the ongoing visa issues and is engaging with the relevant authorities to find a solution.
"We are aware of the UAE visa complications. Discussions are underway with the concerned authorities to resolve the matter," he wrote, adding that the government remains committed to protecting the interests of its citizens.
"If we can do something positive for our expatriates, it will be good both for them and for the government," he said.
Nur acknowledged that the frustration among migrant workers is understandable, attributing it to years of mismanagement and neglect.
He said efforts have been underway since he assumed office to improve the situation.
"Let's see how much we can achieve. It may take time, but I hope we will be able to bring positive changes," he wrote.

item.title: Health minister visits Tala Health Complex, promises upgrade to 100-bed hospital
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain made a surprise visit to Tala Upazila Health Complex in Satkhira on Sunday, inspecting hospital facilities and pledging to upgrade the facility to a 100-bed hospital.
Arriving at around 10:30 am, the minister began his inspection in the hospital kitchen, where he sampled food prepared for patients to assess its quality. He later toured the male and female wards, medicine store, operating theatre (OT), administrative offices, washrooms, and staff attendance registers.
During the visit, he met patients to hear their views on medical treatment, medicine availability, and the overall quality of healthcare services. He also inspected the hospital premises and discussed service challenges and future development plans with local residents and officials.
The minister instructed hospital authorities to improve healthcare services and ordered action against those responsible for the theft of air-conditioning units from the hospital. He also directed officials to expedite ongoing renovation work, including improvements to washroom facilities and called for administrative action against a medical officer who has reportedly remained absent from duty for an extended period.
Speaking to reporters after the visit, Hossain said the government is continuing to recruit doctors through a special Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) process to address staffing shortages. He added that the recruitment process for 100,000 healthcare workers has also begun.
The minister announced that work to upgrade Tala Upazila Health Complex to a 100-bed facility will begin soon, with soil testing expected in the coming weeks.
He said the project includes constructing a modern seven-to- eight-storey building equipped with separate paralysis rehabilitation centers for men and women, a physiotherapy center, a breastfeeding corner, and a trauma center to strengthen healthcare services for the region.

Death toll reaches 43 as 3 more die of dengue in 24 hrs
item.description:
Three people died of dengue and 458 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country in 24 hours until 8:00am on Sunday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 43 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The new deaths were reported in Dhaka South City Corporation, Khulna and Barisal divisions, it said.
During the reporting period, 458 patients were discharged from hospitals after recovery.
Since January 1, a total of 13,098 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country.
Of them, 11,937 have recovered and been discharged, while 1,118 patients are currently undergoing treatment.

item.title: Jamuna erosion keeps Tangail regional road cut off for 6th day
item.description:
Traffic on the Tangail–Bhuapur–Tarakandi regional road remained suspended for the sixth consecutive day yesterday as repair work on a section washed away by erosion from the Jamuna River continued, causing widespread disruption and raising fears of further collapse.
The erosion began suddenly last Sunday at Sakharia village in Gopalpur upazila, where strong currents from the Jamuna River swept away an initial 25-metre stretch of the road. The damaged section has since widened to about 80 metres.
The road closure has halted the movement of passenger buses, freight vehicles and ambulances, forcing commuters and transport operators to use longer alternative routes. The detours have increased travel time, transportation costs and hardship for residents.
People living near the affected area have begun moving household belongings and livestock to safer locations amid concerns that further erosion could breach the remaining road and allow river water to inundate nearby settlements.
Officials from the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) are carrying out emergency protection work by dumping geo bags and tube bags along the eroding riverbank in an effort to stabilise the area.
Locals said they remain anxious despite the ongoing work, warning that failure to contain the erosion quickly could lead to extensive damage to homes, agricultural land and critical infrastructure.
"We are living in constant fear," said local resident Nazrul Islam. "If the road collapses completely, vast areas of Gopalpur, Bhuapur and the greater Mymensingh region could be affected."
Another resident, Md Hayrat, said villagers have been unable to sleep peacefully due to fears that the erosion could destroy their homes and farmland.
A resident named Anowara said her family had already moved their cattle to safer ground and feared they would have nowhere to go if the road gave way completely.
BWDB Executive Engineer Main Uddin attributed the erosion to heavy rainfall, strong upstream flows and changes in the Jamuna's channel caused by the formation of sandbars, which redirected the river's current towards the road.
"The affected section remains vulnerable. Geo bag dumping operations are continuing and will remain in place until the situation is brought under control," he said.
Local lawmaker Abdus Salam Pintu said emergency erosion-control measures were launched immediately after the collapse and that the government, BWDB and local residents were working together to prevent further damage.
The state minister for fisheries and livestock said more than 25,000 geo bags, along with large pipe bags, had already been deployed to reinforce the riverbank. He added that the government was also pursuing plans for a permanent embankment and hoped the emergency repair work would be completed soon.

item.title: Dev projects in Dumuria face uncertainty amid funding crisis
item.description:
Development projects worth around Tk1.70 crore in Dumuria Upazila of Khulna are facing uncertainty as the upazila administration’s development fund has almost run out of money.
The fund crisis has put several projects, including rural road construction, tube wells, religious institutions, educational facilities and other public infrastructure works, at risk of cancellation.
According to the upazila administration records, the development fund had a balance of Tk7.15 crore on 30 July 2025, while the revenue fund stood at Tk35 lakh .
However, at a meeting held on 21 May this year, officials said the balance in the development fund had dropped to only Tk3,729, while the revenue fund had increased to Tk3.30 core.
The figures show that nearly Tk7.15 crore was spent from the development fund within ten months, raising questions among local stakeholders over the utilisation of the money.
Meanwhile, the Upazila Engineering Department’s development projects worth Tk1.70 crore for the 2025–26 fiscal year are now at risk of being stalled due to the shortage of funds.
Contractors have already stopped 54 projects under seven packages, involving around Tk 80 lakh, after failing to receive work orders despite winning tenders through a lottery process held on 21 May.
Some contractors said they had completed assigned works and submitted bills, but later found that there was no money available in the development fund for payment.
The affected projects include road development, tube wells, mosques, temples, madrasas, educational institutions and paving works. Projects worth another Tk90 lakh are still at the tender invitation stage.
Sheikh Shahinur Rahman, president of the Dumuria Upazila Contractor Welfare Association, said contractors had suffered financial losses after spending money to participate in the tender process.
“More than 100 contractors submitted bids for projects under the Upazila Engineering Department. Each contractor spent around Tk7,500 on the tender process. Many won projects through the lottery, but work orders have not been issued,” he said.
He added that a meeting between contractors and the Upazila Executive Officer was held, but no solution had been found.
Dumuria Upazila Engineer Muhammad Darul Huda said the tender process was completed following government regulations, including newspaper advertisements and a lottery system.
“Work orders cannot be issued because there is no money available in the upazila development fund,” he said.
Upazila Executive Officer Sabita Sarkar said issuing work orders without sufficient funds would create further complications.
“If contractors are given work orders, they will complete the projects and submit bills. But there is no money in the fund to pay them,” she said.
Md Kamrul Islam Sardar, executive engineer of the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED), Khulna, said several projects under the 2025–26 fiscal year had been affected due to the fund shortage.
“If work orders are issued without available funds, contractors will complete the work and later face difficulties getting their payments,” he said.
The shortage of funds has raised concerns that important development activities in Dumuria may remain stalled unless additional financial support is arranged.

item.title: Govt primary school enrolment falls in Rajshahi
item.description:
Enrolment in government primary schools across Rajshahi division has declined over the past 12 years despite population growth, while private kindergartens and madrasas have continued to attract more students, according to official data.
Figures from the Divisional Deputy Director's Office of Primary Education show that student enrolment in government primary schools dropped from 1,320,975 in 2014 to 1,183,992 in 2026, a decline of 136,983. During the same period, the population of Rajshahi division increased by around 2.5 million.
In contrast, enrolment in private primary schools, including kindergartens, rose from 436,966 to 504,030 students. Officials also said admissions to Alia and Qawmi madrasas have increased steadily, although consolidated enrolment data were unavailable.
Educationists say the shift reflects growing concerns among parents about the quality of education in government schools, as well as stronger confidence in private institutions.
Head teachers across the division said the rapid expansion of kindergartens and madrasas has contributed significantly to declining enrolment in government schools.
Afroza Khatun, head teacher of Kantanagar Government Primary School in Bagmara upazila, said the school's enrolment had fallen from around 100 students to about 60 after two kindergartens opened nearby.
At Atkoshi Government Primary School in Rajshahi city, enrolment has dropped from more than 550 students five years ago to around 350, according to head teacher Nilufa Akhtar Khanam.
"There are at least 10 kindergarten schools and several madrasas within one kilometre of our school. Many students have transferred there," she said.
Teachers from more than two dozen government primary schools interviewed by this correspondent reported similar trends, with many citing increased admissions to nearby kindergartens and madrasas.
Nikhil Ranjan Pramanik, a teacher at Kachua-2 Government Primary School in Tanore upazila, said 17 students recently left his school to enrol in a nearby madrasa.
"We are trying to improve the quality of education, but admissions continue to decline every year," he said.
Parents said they preferred kindergartens because of regular assessments, closer teacher supervision, better communication with families and greater emphasis on English-language education.
"Government schools are free, but we are not satisfied with the quality of education," said Mustafizur Rahman, a parent in Rajshahi city. "Kindergarten teachers closely monitor children and regularly update parents on their progress."
Another guardian, Saju, whose son attends Shaheen School in Rajshahi, said he chose a private school because he believed it offered better-quality education and stronger English instruction.
Domestic worker Asma Begum said she enrolled her daughter in a kindergarten despite financial hardship because she wanted her to receive a better education.
Professor Dr Akhter Banu, director of the Institute of Education and Research at Rajshahi University, said parents ultimately choose schools they trust.
"Even many government primary school teachers prefer to enrol their own children in private schools instead of the schools where they teach. That reflects declining confidence in the public education system," she said.
She said weak supervision, limited teacher motivation and a lack of accountability have undermined public trust, while private schools maintain closer communication with parents.
"Unless supervision, accountability and teacher motivation improve, parents will continue to shift their children to other institutions," she added.
Nur Akhtar Jannatul Ferdous, assistant director at the Rajshahi Divisional Deputy Director's Office of Primary Education, said more research was needed to determine the reasons behind the decline in enrolment.
"It is not possible to identify a single reason at this stage. A detailed study is needed to understand the factors involved," she said.

item.title: Tangail bridge approach damaged by heavy rainfall
item.description:
Heavy rainfall has damaged a section of the approach to a bridge by the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) at Shyamar Ghat on the Tangail–Hugra road in Tangail Sadar upazila, making vehicular movement risky.
On Sunday afternoon, LGED Executive Engineer Jahanara Parvin, who recently joined the district, inspected the damaged bridge approach and said repairs would be carried out soon.
According to residents, a section of the bridge approach collapsed during the current monsoon season due to heavy rainfall, creating risks for vehicles crossing the bridge.
The bridge is used daily by thousands of people from Hugra, Dyenna, Katuli and Kakua in the char areas of Tangail Sadar upazila, as well as Chauhali in Sirajganj district. Residents said the same section of the approach had collapsed several times in the past and called for a permanent solution.
After being informed about the damage, Jahanara Parvin visited the site and inspected the affected area.
She said: “The bridge approach was damaged due to heavy rainfall. After the inspection, the matter has been reported to the higher authorities. We hope the repairs will be completed quickly so that the bridge becomes suitable for vehicular movement.”
LGED Sub-Assistant Engineer Mostafizur Rahman and other department officials were present during the inspection.
The bridge was constructed around 15 years ago to improve transportation for residents of the surrounding char areas.

item.title: HC sets Aug 2 for verdict on Chinmoy’s bail in 2 cases
item.description:
The High Court on Sunday set August 2 to deliver the verdict on the rule over the bail of Bangladesh Sammilito Sanatani Jagaran Jote spokesperson Chinmoy Krishna Das Brahmachari, also known as Chandan Kumar Dhar, in two cases.
A High Court bench comprising Justice KM Zahid Sarwar Kajol and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher set August 2 for delivering the verdict after concluding the hearing on the rule.
Advocate Apurba Kumar Bhattacharya appeared for Chinmoy Das during the hearing.
Earlier, the High Court had issued a rule asking why Chinmoy Das should not be granted bail in the two vandalism cases.
On October 31, 2024, Firoz Khan, general secretary of the BNP's Mohra Ward unit in Chittagong, filed a sedition case with Kotwali Police Station against Chinmoy Krishna Das and 18 others. Chinmoy Das and several co-accused were subsequently arrested in the case.
Separately, clashes erupted on the Chittagong court premises on November 26, 2025, after a court denied Chinmoy Das bail in the sedition case, allegedly following unrest by his supporters.
During the violence, lawyer Saiful Islam was beaten and hacked to death. Nearly two dozen suspects have since been arrested over the killing, while additional cases were later filed against Chinmoy Das.

item.title: Man to die for killing elderly woman in Narayanganj
item.description:
A Narayanganj court on Sunday sentenced a man to death for killing a 77-year-old woman and stealing her gold jewelry in Rupganj in 2021. Judge Md Abu Shamim Azad of the Narayanganj District and Sessions Judge Court delivered the verdict, also imposing an additional 10 years of rigorous imprisonment for robbery, along with fines totaling Tk 250,000.
The convict, Md Rubel Mia, also known as Rubel Pradhan, was present in court during the judgment.
According to the prosecution, Rubel entered the victim Shafia Begum’s house on January 22, 2021 and fatally attacked her with a sharp weapon before fleeing with a gold chain and earrings.
The victim’s daughter later filed a murder and robbery case with Rupganj Police Station. Police submitted the charge sheet in June 2023, and Rubel later confessed before a magistrate under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Prosecutors said the murder was motivated by Rubel’s need for money to buy drugs. The court delivered the verdict after examining testimony from 12 prosecution witnesses.

item.title: SDF seeks ICT probe into Shahabuddin's alleged role in July killings
item.description:
The State Dialogue Forum (SDF) has submitted a petition to the International Crimes Tribunal, seeking an investigation into the alleged role of former president Mohammed Shahabuddin in the killings during the July 2024 mass uprising, as well as enforced disappearances and torture during the Awami League's rule.
The petition was submitted to the Chief Prosecutor on Sunday by the forum's central member secretary, Al Noor Mohammad Ayas.
In the petition, Ayas alleged that he was abducted by masked men from the Mohakhali bus terminal on the night of January 18, 2025, after leading protests at Shahbagh demanding Shahabuddin's resignation. He claimed he was subjected to physical and psychological torture and was forced to record a video message calling for the suspension of the movement.
According to the petition, he was abandoned near the Kawran Bazar-Banglamotor area the following day and was later rescued and admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Ayas also urged the tribunal to investigate Shahabuddin's alleged role as an instigator of the shootings, killings, enforced disappearances and other alleged human rights abuses against students and civilians during the July 2024 mass uprising.
He further called for an impartial and independent investigation into Shahabuddin's constitutional role and responsibilities as the then president, as well as whether he bore any legal liability or involvement in the 2024 election, alleged human rights violations, and events related to the mass uprising.

item.title: Gas crisis deepens as LNG terminal outage disrupts supply, cripples household cooking
item.description:
The ongoing gas crisis, triggered by a fire at a floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) in Cox’s Bazar, is unlikely to ease anytime soon, leaving millions of households in Dhaka and surrounding areas struggling to cook.
The accident has reduced the country's total gas supply to below 2,150 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), down from an average of around 2,700 mmcfd that had been maintained over the past year, despite the national daily demand standing at nearly 3,800 mmcfd.
The fire at the FSRU operated by Excelerate Energy at Moheshkhali on Tuesday damaged one of its two boilers, forcing it to suspend operations, further plummeting the gas supply.
International expert teams from the UK and the United Arab Emirates have been working at the terminal since Thursday to repair the technical damage.
Tariqul Islam Khan, public relations officer of Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation (Petrobangla), indicated that while efforts are underway, it will take more time before the facility can resume operation.
The severe supply shortfall has hit domestic kitchens the hardest, with gas pressure dropping to near zero or flickering feebly in many parts of the capital.
Residents in areas such as Mohammadpur, Kalabagan, Kafrul, Kazipara, West Tejturi Bazar, Mirpur, Rampura and Badda reported that stoves have remained unlit or unusable for days.
Stripped of regular gas supply, many low-income families have been forced to build temporary clay stoves and cook with firewood. Others who can afford it are turning to costly electric cookers or LPG cylinders, significantly increasing their daily household expenses.
Frustrated residents in several neighbourhoods, including Mohammadpur, have staged demonstrations and vented their anger on social media platforms over the persistent cooking crisis.
Beyond domestic kitchens, the shortage has severely impacted other sectors.
According to Petrobangla, gas-fired electricity generation has fallen by approximately 1,500 megawatts, raising concerns over widespread power cuts.
Long queues of vehicles have formed at CNG filling stations across the city, while industrial production has slowed down due to low gas pressure.
Petrobangla issued a statement apologising to consumers for the unexpected disruption and assured that technical teams are working continuously to restore the terminal.
Meanwhile, Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution PLC warned that low gas pressure will persist across Dhaka and adjacent districts until the situation improves.

item.title: Bangladeshi artist wins gold prize at World Beauty Art & Design International Contest
item.description:
Bangladeshi artist Sayma Sadia won the gold prize in the Makeup – General Category at the 25th World Beauty Art & Design International Contest, held in Seoul, South Korea.
Organized by the World Beauty Art Association, the annual competition brings together beauty artists, educators, and professionals from around the world to showcase their work in makeup, beauty, and artistic design.
According to officials at the award ceremony, Sayma received the gold prize in recognition of her artistic skill, creativity, and technical expertise in the Makeup – General Category.
Sayma is currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Beauty Design at Woosong University in South Korea. She said the award marked a significant milestone in her career and encouraged her to pursue higher goals in the global beauty industry.
She hopes to work with internationally recognized beauty and cosmetics brands while specializing in Special Effects (SFX) Makeup, a field widely used in film, television, fashion, and theater.
Speaking about the achievement, Sayma said: “I feel deeply honored and grateful to receive this recognition. Winning the gold prize is not just my achievement, it belongs to everyone who has supported me throughout my journey. At this moment, I especially remember my parents and my sister, whose love, encouragement, and sacrifices have helped me reach this stage. Their belief in me has always been my greatest strength.”
Her achievement reflects the growing presence of Bangladeshi talent in international beauty and design competitions and highlights the country's expanding participation in the global creative industry.

Faridpur farmers expect bumper jute harvest, seek fair prices
item.description:
Farmers in Faridpur are busy harvesting and retting jute cultivated on 87,000 hectares this season, with favourable weather boosting hopes of bumper yield. However, growers remain concerned over rising production costs and uncertainty surrounding market prices.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), nearly 90% of farmers in the district cultivated jute this season. The production target has been set at 195,000 metric tonnes, with an expected average yield of 2.24 metric tonnes per hectare.
DAE Deputy Director Shahaduzzaman said favourable weather conditions throughout the growing season have increased the likelihood of achieving the production target.
"We are optimistic about meeting this season's target as weather conditions have remained favourable for jute cultivation," he said.
He added that Faridpur contributes around 30% of the country's total jute production, with the district's fibre widely recognised for its quality.
Despite the positive production outlook, farmers say higher input costs have squeezed their profit margins. Limited rainfall at the beginning of the season forced many to irrigate their fields, while rising prices of fertilisers, fuel and other agricultural inputs increased cultivation expenses. Labour costs have also continued to climb.
Farmers in Saltha, including Hasem Matubbar, Harun Molla and Saiful Islam, said they are currently harvesting and retting their crop but fear incurring losses if they do not receive fair prices at the end of the season.
They urged the government to procure jute at the announced price on time and improve market management to ensure fair returns, saying such measures would encourage farmers to expand jute cultivation.
Faridpur Farmers' Association President Manik Majumdar said strong production alone would not guarantee farmers' livelihoods.
"Ensuring fair prices, improving market access and reducing production costs are essential to making jute cultivation profitable," he said. "That will help preserve Faridpur's position as one of Bangladesh's leading jute-producing districts."

item.title: Heavy rains push up vegetable, fish prices in Gopalganj
item.description:
Prices of vegetables in Gopalganj have doubled or even tripled over the past 10 days following heavy rainfall that damaged crops and disrupted supplies, leaving low and middle-income families struggling to cope with soaring food costs.
A visit to Boro Bazar in the town showed that no vegetable was selling for less than Tk 60 per kilogram. Okra, previously priced at Tk 20-25 per kg, is now selling for Tk 60. Sweet pumpkin price has increased from Tk 25-30 to Tk 60, while pointed gourd, ridge gourd and teasel gourd are selling at Tk 80 per kg after rising sharply from Tk 30-35. Sponge gourd now costs Tk 60, and both bitter gourd and taro corms have reached Tk 80 per kg.
A medium-sized bottle gourd that recently sold for Tk 30-40 now costs Tk 80-100. Papaya remains the cheapest vegetable at Tk 40 per kg, while green chilies have jumped to Tk 200 per kg from Tk 80 just 10 days ago.
Fish prices have also climbed significantly. Hilsa weighing one kilogram is selling for nearly Tk 3,000, while smaller hilsa weighing 350-400 grams costs around Tk 1,500. Farmed varieties, including pangas, rohit, catla and silver carp, have become Tk 25-50 more expensive per kilogram. Rohit now sells for Tk 500-600 per kg, up from Tk 450-480 only a few days ago.
Fish trader Johor blamed the increase on heavy rains in fish-producing areas, saying floodwaters caused farmed fish to escape from ponds, reducing market supply. Although hilsa prices briefly declined last week due to increased seasonal catches, they have since risen again, pushing overall fish prices higher.
Consumers say the rising costs are placing severe pressure on household budgets. Shopper Saidul Islam Shovon said many families can no longer afford to buy all the essentials. Another customer, Md. Ehsanul Alam, said his family has reduced fish consumption because prices continue to rise while incomes remain unchanged.
Vegetable traders said continuous rainfall has damaged crops and sharply reduced supplies reaching wholesale markets. They noted that vegetable prices usually increase during the monsoon season, but this year's prolonged rainfall has made the situation far worse.
Dr. Md. Mamunur Rahman, Deputy Director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Gopalganj, said above-normal rainfall in July inundated 85 hectares of vegetable fields, damaging crops including bitter gourd, bottle gourd, pumpkin, papaya, pointed gourd, okra, chili and yardlong beans. The losses have affected 1,360 vegetable farmers and significantly reduced local market supplies.
District Agricultural Marketing Officer Arif Hossain said authorities are continuing regular market monitoring and have advised traders to avoid excessive profit-taking while maintaining reasonable margins between wholesale and retail prices.
He added that with local production declining, most vegetables are now being brought into Gopalganj from other districts, contributing to higher prices.

item.title: Youth found dead at Hasina’s residence Sudha Sadan in Dhanmondi
item.description:
Police recovered the hanging body of a 20-year-old man from Sudha Sadan, the former residence of ex-prime minister Sheikh Hasina in the Dhanmondi area of the capital on Saturday.
The deceased was identified as Shakil, son of Sekandar Ali Matubbar and Asma Begum. He lived in the Shibpur Tile Office area of Jigatola under Mohammadpur.
Police said the body was recovered at around 11am after locals informed them. It was later sent to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy following due procedures.
Md Waduzzaman, sub-inspector (SI) of Dhanmondi Police Station, said the body was found hanging with a noose around the neck.
He said the Crime Scene Unit of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) identified the deceased through fingerprint analysis.
The exact cause of death has not yet been determined, and an investigation is underway, the police officer added.

item.title: Pipe bomb planted to target Rath Yatra
item.description:
The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit said the pipe bomb had been planted to target the Ulto Rath Yatra procession after police recovered the powerful improvised explosive device (IED) beneath Motijheel Metro Rail Station in Dhaka on Friday.
Sub-Inspector (SI) Mirza Mohammad Mukta of Motijheel Police Station subsequently filed a case under the Explosives Act against unidentified individuals
According to the case, police received information about a suspicious bomb-like object along the procession route and recovered an umbrella containing a powerful pipe bomb before the religious procession reached the area. Authorities said the device was detected in time, preventing a potentially serious incident.
A passerby was injured during the controlled disposal of the bomb on Friday night. The injured, 66-year-old Miraj Ahmed, an employee of the Ministry of Education, sustained splinter injuries to his left eye. After receiving primary treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, he was referred to the National Institute of Ophthalmology in Agargaon for further treatment.
According to the case documents, SI Mirza Mohammad Mukta was on duty with the "Honda Mobile" patrol unit to provide security for the Ulto Rath Yatra procession.
The procession began at Dhakeshwari National Temple, passed through Shapla Chattar in Motijheel and was scheduled to conclude at Swamibagh Ashram.
During the evening, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Control Room received information from the Traffic Division about a suspicious bomb-like object near the procession route. The device had been concealed inside an umbrella, and witnesses reported seeing a blinking light on it.
Following instructions from senior officials, SI Mukta and other officers reached the area beside the generator room of Motijheel Metro Rail Station at around 6:20pm and secured the location where the device had been found.
Police then requested participants in the procession to avoid the area, telling them there had been an electrical short circuit, allowing the procession to continue safely toward Swamibagh Ashram.
After the procession had passed through the area, members of the DMP Bomb Disposal Unit carried out a controlled explosion and safely neutralized the device, according to the case.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Saturday evening, Additional Commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police and chief of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit Mohammad Shamsul Haque said: "The powerful pipe bomb had been planted to target the Rath Yatra procession."
He said the explosive had been attached to an umbrella in a way that opening it would have triggered the blast, potentially causing multiple casualties.
Describing the device, he said: "It was an improvised explosive device (IED) in the form of a pipe bomb. It contained sulfur, a large quantity of sharp metal fragments and barbed wire. The device was connected to a battery and an electrical circuit and was designed so that pressing the release button to open the umbrella would detonate the bomb."
Shamsul Haque confirmed that one passerby was injured during the bomb disposal operation and said the casualties could have been much higher had the area been crowded.
He added that investigators have yet to identify those responsible or determine their motive. He urged the public not to panic, saying law enforcement agencies and other relevant authorities are investigating the incident to identify and apprehend those involved.

item.title: 439 fresh cases of dengue infection reported, 1 death overnight
item.description:
Health officials on Saturday said they recorded 439 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts killing at least one person in the past 24 hours.
"During the period, (of the 439) 83 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division while 75 in Chittagong division, 77 in Dhaka division, 46 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 41 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 41 in Khulna division, 19 in Mymensingh division, 26 in Rajshahi division, 30 in Rangpur division and one Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts Bangladesh this year witnessed, so far, 40 deaths while the disease inflicted 12,640.
The dengue last year claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, the mosquito-borne disease claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

Gazette of president’s resignation published
item.description:
According to Article 54 of the Constitution, Speaker of the National Parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram will discharge the duties of the president of the People's Republic of Bangladesh until a new president is elected.
The provision came into effect following the resignation of President Mohammed Sahabuddin from office on Friday.
The Cabinet Division on Saturday issued a gazette notification in this regard.
The gazette, signed by Cabinet Secretary Dr Nasimul Gani, stated that the order would be implemented immediately in accordance with the Constitution.
The Cabinet Division's website has also published the gazette confirming acceptance of the resignation letter of outgoing President Mohammed Sahabuddin and stating that Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram will discharge the responsibilities of the president as the new head of state.

item.title: Tea workers block highway demanding Tk500 daily wage
item.description:
Tea garden workers in Sylhet blocked the Sylhet-Tamabil highway and staged demonstrations on Saturday morning, demanding a daily minimum wage of Tk500.
The demonstration, organised by the Tea Workers Trade Union Centre, was a large protest rally that took place at the Khadim Tea Garden around 9:30am. During the program, workers observed a two-hour work stoppage and staged a blockade on the Highway.
They also demanded the cancellation of the controversial 5% pay-hike gazette, land ownership rights, and elections for the Tea Workers Union (CBA).
Expressing deep resentment, speakers noted that the current wage structure is extremely inhumane given the surging prices of essential commodities. They described the annual wage increase of just Tk8 as a "farce and mockery" against the tea workers. Speakers stated that it is impossible for a family to survive on the current daily wage of just Tk187, making a dignified and fair wage a core demand for tea labourers across the country.
Addressing land rights, leaders highlighted that despite living in the region for nearly 200 years, tea workers remain landless. The absence of land ownership deprives them of basic civil amenities and constitutional rights, making guaranteed land ownership an urgent necessity.
SM Shuvo, chief coordinator of the organization, urged workers across all gardens to unite in the struggle for a Tk500 daily wage.
Earlier in the morning, a large protest procession began from the Loha Pool area of Khadim Tea Garden, marching through various roads within the estate before occupying the Sylhet-Tamabil Highway.
Chaired by Tea Workers Trade Union Centre President Sabuj Tanti and moderated by Coordinator Manisha Wahid, the rally was addressed by Chief Coordinator SM Shuvo, Adviser Syed Farhad Hossain, Office Secretary Dipto Nayek, and Burjan Tea Factory worker leader Sushanta Chasha, among others.

item.title: Formal charges in Shapla Chattar case to be filed on Monday
item.description:
The prosecution will submit formal charges to the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Monday in the crimes against humanity case over the alleged killings during the 2013 Shapla Chattar operation, Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said on Saturday.
Speaking at a discussion titled "Human Rights Violations and Access to Justice for Victims" at the CIRDAP auditorium in Dhaka, Aminul Islam said the ICT's investigation agency had completed its probe into the events of May 5, 2013, and submitted its report to the Chief Prosecutor's Office.
After reviewing the findings, prosecutors prepared the formal charge sheet, which will be placed before the tribunal on Monday, marking the next stage in the judicial process, he said.
According to the prosecution, more than 40 people, including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, have been named as accused in the case. The full list of defendants will be disclosed when the formal charges are filed.
Nine people are currently in custody in connection with the case. They include former minister Dr Dipu Moni, former state minister for home affairs Shamsul Haque Tuku, retired Major General Ziaul Ahsan, former inspector general of police AKM Shahidul Hoque, former deputy inspector general Mollah Nazrul Islam, Shahriar Kabir, president of the advisory committee of the Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee, former DIG Abdul Jalil Mondal, and journalists Farzana Rupa and Mozammel Babu.
Prosecution sources said the investigation report names 41 accused, including Sheikh Hasina, former army chief General Aziz Ahmed, journalists Mozammel Babu and Farzana Rupa, and writer Shahriar Kabir. Detailed information is expected to be disclosed at a formal press briefing.
On May 5, 2013, Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh staged a rally at Shapla Chattar in Dhaka's Motijheel, demanding implementation of its 13-point charter.
Following a day of tensions and clashes, members of the police, Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) carried out a joint overnight operation to clear the area. Allegations that numerous people were killed during the operation later prompted an investigation by the International Crimes Tribunal into possible crimes against humanity.

item.title: Acting President Hafiz to work from Bangabhaban, stay at parliament residence
item.description:
Acting President and Speaker of Parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmed will carry out his official duties from Bangabhaban while continuing to reside at the Speaker's official residence within the National Parliament complex.
Speaking to the media on Saturday, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed confirmed the matter.
Special security measures have been in place since Friday afternoon at the Speaker's official residence and surrounding areas as part of the Acting President's security protocol.
The Speaker assumed the role of Acting President on Friday under the Constitution after President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned, citing health reasons.
According to Shairul Kabir Khan, the Acting President will begin his official engagements on Sunday. At 11:00 am, he will lay a wreath at the National Martyrs' Memorial in Savar to pay tribute to the country's fallen heroes.
He will then visit the graves of martyred President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar at 12:30 pm to pay his respects and offer prayers.

item.title: Law minister: All must be treated with equal dignity, not divided by religion
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Saturday said there is no need to identify or divide people on the basis of religion, stressing that every citizen of Bangladesh must be treated with equal dignity and equal rights.
"Just as a person's blood does not change color because of their religion, citizens' rights cannot vary on religious grounds either. If we can value and respect everyone as human beings, only then will it be possible to eliminate communal divisions and discrimination," he said.
The law minister said this while speaking as the chief guest at the biennial conference of the Mohanogor Sarbojanin Puja Committee held at the premises of the Dhakeshwari National Temple in the capital on Saturday noon.
He said Bangladesh should be built as a country where every citizen naturally feels safe and can celebrate religious festivals without fear or disruption.
"The minister said everyone must refrain from using religion for politics or electoral gains. Instead, politics should be guided by a commitment to public welfare, development, good governance and human values. The present government's goal is to create an environment in which every citizen can practice his or her religion freely and without hindrance," he added.
Referring to the encroachment on the land of the Dhakeshwari National Temple, the law minister said the government would take the necessary steps to recover the occupied property.
He said no land grabber, criminal or mafia syndicate would be allowed to retain possession of the temple's property permanently and assured the authorities of the government's full cooperation in this regard.
Prime Minister's Special Assistant on Hindu, Buddhist, Christian and Ethnic Minority Affairs Bijon Kanti Sarkar, Dhaka-7 lawmaker Hamidur Rahman, Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad President Basudeb Dhar, its General Secretary Santosh Sharma, Mohanogor Sarbojanin Puja Committee President Jayanta Kumar Dev, its General Secretary Dr Tapas Chandra Pal, and leaders of the Dhakeshwari National Temple Management Committee addressed the function, among others.

item.title: Fakhrul: Research, innovation should be prioritized over political debate
item.description:
LGRD and Cooperatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir Saturday said research, innovation and productive activities should be given priority instead of political debate.
The outcomes of research must reach the field level to increase farmers’ income and further strengthen the rural economy, he said.
The minister made the remarks while addressing the inaugural ceremony of the “36th Annual Planning Conference-2026” as the chief guest at the Rural Development Academy (RDA) in Bogra, said a PID release.
Earlier, he visited the green technology exhibition developed by the RDA and planted a sapling of a Burmese grape tree.
The minister said although political discussions dominate in the country, the achievements in research and innovation do not receive due importance, even though technologies developed by researchers can play a significant role in increasing farmers’ productivity.
He called upon the media to highlight such achievements more extensively.
He said the biggest problem facing farmers is not production, but ensuring fair prices for their produce.
The minister also stressed increasing research on the development of cold storage, preservation and marketing systems alongside encouraging private investment in the sector.
Urging young people to become entrepreneurs, the minister further said that instead of only pursuing jobs, they should engage in agriculture-based initiatives as well as preservation and marketing systems, which would create employment opportunities while benefiting farmers.
Rural Development and Cooperatives Division Secretary Mohammad Showkat Rashid Chowdhury chaired the function, which was attended, among others, by Bogra-5 lawmaker Golam Mohammad Siraj, Bogra-1 lawmaker Kazi Rafiqul Islam, Senior Secretary of the Ministry of Public Administration Md Ehsanul Haque and other concerned officials.

item.title: PM, navy chief discuss maritime security, modernization
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and newly appointed Chief of Naval Staff Vice-Admiral Khondkar Misbah ul Azim on Saturday discussed maritime security, the modernization of the Bangladesh Navy, and ways to enhance its professional capabilities during a meeting at the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) in Dhaka.
The two also exchanged views on other related issues, Prime Minister's Assistant Press Secretary Gazi Shahriar Pamir said.
The prime minister lauded the professionalism of the Bangladesh Navy and its role in safeguarding the country's sovereignty. He wished the newly appointed chief of naval staff success in carrying out his responsibilities.
Vice-Admiral Khondkar Misbah ul Azim expressed his gratitude to the prime minister during the courtesy call.

item.title: Rizvi: BNP high command to decide on next president
item.description:
Prime Minister's Political Adviser and BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Saturday said the party's top leadership will decide who will be the country's next president.
He made the remarks after paying tributes at the graves of martyred president Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Khaleda Zia at Zia Udyan in the capital, along with the newly appointed chairmen of 12 state-owned institutions.
Responding to a question about the next president, Rizvi said the matter would be decided by the party's high command.
He also said the demand raised by various political parties for the trial of the resigned president is a matter of party policy.
Rizvi expressed hope that the newly appointed chairmen of the state-owned institutions would discharge their responsibilities with honesty and dedication.
He also added that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is evaluating and rewarding party leaders and activists who made sacrifices at different levels.
During this period, Shahabuddin administered the oath of office to three heads of government, an exceptional occurrence in the country's history for a sitting president.

Houthis say hit Saudi Arabia as Trump weighs harder Iran strikes
item.description:
Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on Saudi Arabia on Saturday as US President Donald Trump mulled fresh strikes on the Islamic Republic in the deepening Middle East war.
Houthi media said the rebels targeted the Saudi City of Jizan on the Red Sea and Saudi’s civil defense issued warnings in the area on the kingdom’s southwest coast as well as in Yanbu to the north.
A post by Ansarollah media on Telegram said the strike had sparked fires and a video circulating on social media, and verified by AFP, showed dark clouds rising above a refinery belonging to Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco in Jizan.
Earlier, the Iran-backed group accused US ally Saudi Arabia of a “dangerous escalation” after Riyadh struck Houthi targets on Friday.
A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets.
The renewed exchange of fire between the US and Iranian allies signals the emergence of a new front in the Middle East war following US and Israeli strikes on Iran at the end of February.
Faiza, a 36-year-old mother of two and Hodeida resident, told AFP the strikes were like “the sound of loud thunder,” explaining she had heard three distinct explosions.
“I didn’t want to believe that we had gone back to strikes,” she added.
Yemen’s Houthis have been at war with the internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government since 2015 in a devastating conflict that has killed hundreds of thousands and triggered a major humanitarian crisis.
However, fighting in the poverty-stricken Arabian peninsula country had been largely been frozen since a UN-negotiated truce in 2022.
This week the Houthis announced a maritime blockade of the top oil producer, hitting Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.
The threat to shipping comes in parallel to Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the central flash point between Tehran and Washington amid renewed hostilities between the two sides.
On Saturday, the US did not announce strikes on Iran for the first time after 13 consecutive nights of bombardments against the Islamic Republic.
Trump said he had not yet decided whether to launch major strikes on Iran, hours before the escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, because Tehran was now getting “serious” in talks with Washington.
“No I haven’t,” Trump told journalists in the Oval Office when asked if he had made a decision on hitting Iran hard.
“Look, we’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.”
Trump said Iran had a choice between making a deal or facing a “much higher level” of strikes, after nearly two weeks of US attacks that have left an April ceasefire in tatters.
The war that Trump once predicted would last four or five weeks is now nearing its fifth month, and is weighing on the Republican’s approval ratings ahead of crucial US midterm elections in November.
Trump added that he did not know what the “tipping point” would be for a decision, but reiterated that his red line would be if Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon.
The United States says it is carrying out the strikes to stop Iran closing the crucial Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has responded with strikes on US bases that have killed four service members.
The Iranian military said Friday it had carried out attacks targeting US military assets in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said they had targeted an Amazon data center in Bahrain, according to state media, though neither the US tech giant nor Bahrain has commented on the claim.
There was also no confirmation from the United States of any targeting of its facilities or personnel.

item.title: Phone line, security in place as Shahabuddin prepares to leave
item.description:
A new telephone line is being installed at the Gulshan residence where outgoing President Mohammed Shahabuddin is expected to move after leaving Bangabhaban.
On Friday afternoon, employees of the Bangladesh Telecommunications Company Limited (BTCL) arrived to install the connection.
According to security guards at the building, Shahabuddin is expected to reside on the fifth floor after stepping down. They said he visited the residence 3 to 4 days ago, accompanied by more than 100 people, including members of law enforcement agencies.
Sources said minor renovation and other preparation work at the residence has already been completed. Several members of the Special Branch (SB) are also stationed there.
Abdur Razzak, a Telecommunications Mechanic (TCM) at Bangladesh Telecommunications Company Limited (BTCL), said the installation was being carried out following official instructions. He said: “We have officially been sent here to install a new telephone line. The previous line was disconnected after he became President. Therefore, we are now installing a new one.”
President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned from office, and his resignation letter was accepted by Speaker of the National Parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmed. The letter was submitted to the speaker on Friday.
In the resignation letter, Shahabuddin said he was stepping down due to serious illness.
